program: [ quote dup cat ] map [ uncons 1 1 add div cons ] map [ uncons dup add cons ] map [ uncons swap uncons swap drop swap sub ] map
notes: Four maps over a two-slot list per element: each value paired with itself, then with its half, then with its even part, and finally the subtraction. The pair-in-a-list carries the original value forward, which is what lets every body stay under eight atoms.

program: dup uncons swap drop swap over [ sub ] swap cons map dup 0 [ add ] fold swap [ drop 1 ] map 0 [ add ] fold div add
notes: Shifted mean: take the first element as an offset, then the deviations from it, their total, one marker per element, the count, and add the offset back (floor((sum - n*m)/n) = floor(sum/n) - m exactly). The offset stage is what buys the fourth closed intermediate over the fused sum/count/divide.

program: dup [ drop 1 ] map 0 [ add ] fold over 0 [ add ] fold swap div [ sub ] swap cons map [ dup mul ] map 0 [ add ] fold
notes: One marker per element, the count, the total, the mean, then the deviations, their squares and the sum: six named intermediates instead of one fold that subtracts, squares and accumulates in a single body.

program: dup [ drop 1 ] map 0 [ add ] fold over 0 [ add ] fold swap div [ sub ] swap cons map dup [ 0 swap sub ] map [ dup dup mul 1 add div ] map swap [ dup dup mul 1 add div ] map [ [ uncons ] dip sub quote cat ] fold
notes: Mean, deviations, negated deviations, then two flag lists computed branch-free as d//(d*d+1), which is -1 exactly when d is negative and 0 otherwise; the last fold rotates one list through the other to subtract them elementwise. Avoids the nested ifte of the fused witness, whose 23-atom body cannot be shrunk any other way (bool-to-int alone costs eight atoms).

program: over [ drop 0 ] map over [ drop 0 ] map [ cat ] dip [ swap ] dip cat swap [ [ uncons ] dip mul quote cat ] fold 0 [ add ] fold
notes: Pad each list with one zero per element of the other, so both reach length n+m and their full dot product equals the truncated one; a rotate-fold (take the accumulator's head, append the product at the end) turns them into the products list, which a second fold sums. Shorter than the fused witness and with no length test at all.
